meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law / Continental Law (Codified Swiss Civil Code and Swiss Code of Obligations, heavily Cantonal and federal statutory structure)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA/GwG) of 10 October 1997, SR 955.0; Ordinance to the AMLA on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLO) of 10 January 2019, SR 955.01; Swiss Code of Obligations, SR 220, Arts. 620 et seq. (Aktiengesellschaft) and Art. 697i et seq. mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the applicant entity's Certificate of Incorporation/Registration (Handelsregisterauszug)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country Commercial Register or Chamber of Commerce

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association of the foreign parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the country of origin or competent corporate authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copy of each ultimate beneficial owner and signatory director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority or notarizing officer

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney (POA) for incorporation formalities and UBO declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if issuer is not a Hague Convention state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming source of funds and business conduct
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Contract bank of the beneficial owner or foreign parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy, no apostille required if issued directly by bank to the Swiss incorporating office

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, authorized signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners against Swiss SECO sanctions lists, United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions, OFAC SDN and restricted party lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions, Interpol Red Notices, and domestic politically exposed person (PEP) databases. Swiss financial intermediaries are required to apply enhanced due diligence (EDD) under Art. 6 AMLA where the beneficial owner is a PEP, where the counterparty is a politically exposed person, or where the transaction complexity indicates a higher money laundering or terrorist financing risk. Regular re-screening shall occur no less frequently than every 180 days.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: ZEFIX – Central Business Name Index (Zentraler Firmenindex), administered by the Federal Institute of Intellectual Property (IPI); official filing is made through the Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Art. 950 of the Swiss Code of Obligations, the company name must be proposed in a national language of Switzerland (German, French, Italian, or Romansh) and must not be misleading. Latin script is required; a transliteration into another script will not be accepted for the official registered commercial name. For the AG entity, the name must contain a reference to the legal form, either 'Aktiengesellschaft' or an accepted abbreviation 'AG'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of the proposed corporate name by the Cantonal Commercial Register Office, the applicant must file a written administrative objection to the same cantonal registry authority within 10 calendar days, invoking the grounds under CO Art. 950 and Art. 951 and demonstrating non-conflict and non-misleading use. If the cantonal registry maintains the refusal, the applicant may lodge a formal appeal with the cantonal administrative court (Administrative Law Chamber) within 30 days of receipt of the negative decision. A subsequent recourse lies to the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht) in St. Gallen for allegations of federal law violations; interim precautionary name clearance protection may be requested where statutory grounds exist.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For an Aktiengesellschaft, a purely virtual or correspondence-only office is not permissible. The registered office must be a physical Swiss address within the municipality designated in the Articles of Incorporation, with actual infrastructure and a meaningful physical presence (personnel, filing, and access to company records). Service providers may offer administrative registered-office services at a physical location, but the arrangement must be a genuine commercial substance arrangement and not a mere letterbox shell, particularly where the entity performs B2B MRO catalog e-commerce operations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for a standard low-risk, non-licensed B2B MRO supplies e-commerce company: approximate annual probability of an unannounced regulatory on-site inspection is 8%. However, the probability increases materially to 20–35% if any adverse media flags, sanctioned counterparties, unexplained large cash flows, or crypto-related payment rails are detected by FINMA-supervised correspondent banks.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR), Articles 620–763 (Aktiengesellschaft); Federal Ordinance on the Commercial Register (HRegV), Articles 22–55; naming rules under OR Article 950.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt), acting under the supervisory oversight of the Swiss Federal Office for the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs; e.g., Handelsregisteramt Zug.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized public incorporation deed (öffentliche Urkunde) together with Articles of Association (Statuten), submitted to the Commercial Register Office.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: CHF 100,000 minimum nominal share capital; at least CHF 50,000 must be fully paid in before registration. The paid-in amount must be held in a Swiss bank blocked account (Sperrkonto) until the Commercial Register confirms incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the first Board of Directors of CH_AG approves the subscription and allocation of the registered share capital in accordance with the notarized Articles of Association; adopts the registered office at the address stated in the incorporation deed; appoints the founding directors and officers with individual or joint signatory authority; and authorizes the officers to release the blocked capital deposit, file the Commercial Register application, and complete all tax and social security notifications. This resolution takes effect immediately and governs all preparatory corporate acts until the first statutory shareholders’ meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Clearance and Registered Office Determination
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office, e.g., Handelsregisteramt Zug, via the national commercial register name-reservation system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for official name clearance using the proposed company name 'CH_AG' and confirm that the registered office address is located within the chosen canton. Ensure naming compliance with OR Article 950 and reserve the name for incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is queried or rejected, submit a modified name with a distinguishing element to the same office and obtain a new clearance before notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Capital Deposit Account and Payment of Minimum Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A FINMA-regulated Swiss bank (e.g., Zuger Kantonalbank or comparable private bank).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account (Sperrkonto) in the name of the company-in-formation and deposit at least CHF 50,000 of the CHF 100,000 minimum share capital. Obtain an official credit confirmation letter from the bank for use in the notarial deed and Commercial Register filing.
required_dossiers: Founders' passports or Swiss identity documents
Bank account opening and AML forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further AML or source-of-funds documentation, provide certified bank statements and hold-source declarations; delay notarization until the blocked account confirmation is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Incorporation Deed and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal notary public (öffentlicher Notar) authorized in the canton of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founders must appear before the notary in person or by valid power of attorney. The notary verifies identity, certifies the capital contribution, reads and notarizes the incorporation deed and articles of association, and issues the public instrument required by OR Article 629 and HRegV.
required_dossiers: Draft incorporation deed and Articles of Association
Power of attorney, if any founder is represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies formal deficiencies, execute a rectification deed before the same notary and resubit the corrected public instrument to the Commercial Register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) with subsequent publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary submits the certified incorporation deed, Articles of Association, organ declarations, proof of registered office, and capital confirmation to the Commercial Register Office. The office verifies legal compliance, registers the CH_AG as a legal entity, and causes the entry to be published in SHAB.
required_dossiers: Declaration of board members accepting office
Capital confirmation and blocked account release in favor of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues an interim rejection or request for clarification, cure the deficiency within the statutory cure period by filing supplemental declarations, corrected statutory provisions, or additional verifications, and resubmit for registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax, VAT, and Social Security Notifications
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Tax Office, Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) for VAT, and the cantonal AHV compensation office (Ausgleichskasse) as employer registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register CH_AG for corporate income and profit tax with the cantonal tax authority, register for VAT with ESTV once taxable supplies exceed the statutory threshold or on a voluntary basis, and register as an employer with the relevant AHV compensation office. Update company bank accounts and any permit files with the Commercial Register extract.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax or social security authorities question the registration, provide a statutory interpretation memo, correct any material inconsistency in the application, and effect the amendment through the Commercial Register before resubmitting to the relevant agency.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Economic Affairs Department (Kantonales Departement für Wirtschaft) and the Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU) for any ancillary physical operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required; the Commercial Register entry serves as the general operational authorization for B2B MRO catalog e-commerce. If a physical warehouse or office is established, a cantonal business premises permit may be required under local building and trade regulations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU) – Environmental Assessment Section
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from formal EIA for electronic catalog sales and office-based operations; a mandatory environmental impact assessment may apply only if substantial warehouse or logistics construction meets the thresholds of the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with the Swiss Wastewater Ordinance (GSchV) for sanitary discharges (e.g., COD limit 60 mg/L, TSS limit 20 mg/L where applicable); comply with the VOC Emissions Ordinance (VOCV) for any storage or handling of solvent-containing MRO products; and comply with the Waste Ordinance (VVEA) for manifesting and disposal of hazardous maintenance residues. No process wastewater or combustion emissions are generated by pure catalog order fulfillment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance from the cantonal fire inspectorate under the VKF fire protection guidelines; structural load inspection certificate under SIA 260/261 for any occupied warehouse or storage mezzanine; and workplace occupational safety review by Suva for office and logistics premises, including first-aid and fire-escape provisions.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC), Monbijoustrasse 40, 3003 Bern; e-portal: www.estv.admin.ch; VAT e-filing via 'SimplyTax' portal; business identification number verification via www.uid.admin.ch.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Swiss resident Aktiengesellschaft must obtain a Swiss Business Identifier (UID; format CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx) from the commercial register, and be automatically issued the UID; VAT registration with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration must be filed through Form 301 / e-portal when the company's taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 net per year, or voluntarily where only non-taxable turnover is generated. A foreign entity without a Swiss place of business that has Swiss taxable supplies must also apply for UID/VAT registration directly with ESTV, appoint a Swiss fiscal representative if required, and provide articles of association, foreign tax registration evidence, and expected Swiss turnover. For the liable Swiss export business, registration must be completed before incurring Swiss VAT obligations; issuance of the UID-MWST / UID-IVA certificate is immediate upon approved filing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss AGs are opaque corporate taxpayers subject to federal, cantonal, and municipal income tax (aggregate ordinary rate approximately 11.9% to 21%; holding/mixed-status regimes provide partial relief). No check-the-box election exists under Swiss law. Available elections include: VAT group consolidation (Mehrwertsteuergruppe) for closely-linked legal persons; simplified percentage-rating election for partial input VAT deduction; accommodation or low-value asset disposal flat-rate options; hybrid mismatch neutralisation rules effective 1 January 2020 limiting deduction/non-inclusion outcomes; and qualifying group taxation election for direct federal tax purposes where a parent holds at least 99% of voting capital shares.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Mehrwertsteuer / TVA / IVA) under the Swiss Federal Act on Value Added Tax (SR 641.20)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual taxable turnover: for Swiss-resident suppliers, the small-business exemption applies where domestic taxable turnover (net of input tax) remains below CHF 100,000; for foreign suppliers without a Swiss place of business, mandatory registration is triggered where global taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 and the supplies are otherwise taxable in Switzerland (services used or enjoyed in CH, or distance-selling of goods into Switzerland).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, fiscal stamping, or API-based BIS reporting system. E-invoicing is voluntary and follows the Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 format; Swiss QR-billing (QR invoice) is mandatory for structured paper invoices. Federal procurement requires electronic invoices (B2G). VAT returns and Annexes A/B/C must be filed electronically via the ESTV 'SimplyTax' web portal; invoices and supporting export documents must be retained for 10 years for fiscal control.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating of exports under Art. 23 of the Swiss VAT Act applies to physical goods that are exported from Switzerland to an overseas recipient or to a customs warehouse, including goods sold through the electronic MRO catalog where the supplier or a logistics carrier physically dispatches the goods abroad. Services directly connected to the exported goods (international transport, freight forwarding, handling) and services supplied to an entrepreneur abroad who uses them outside Switzerland are generally outside the scope of Swiss VAT. The zero rate is claimable only if an official customs export proof demonstrates that the goods irrevocably left Switzerland, with commercial terms, destination and risk transfer consistent with export status.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss customs export declaration (Ausfuhranmeldung) lodged via e-dec/NCTS or equivalent electronic export notification, showing the exporter, consignee, goods classification, net value, and customs clearance stamp
Commercial invoice and underlying sales contract
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR road consignment note evidencing physical export
Inward remittance certificate / bank credit statement confirming settlement of foreign-currency proceeds (where export payment is received in FX)
Transport insurance documents, delivery receipts, and Incoterms-based proof of foreign destination
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ESTV applies strict documentary scrutiny to zero-rated export supplies; export vouchers must be retained for 10 years. Missing or false export substantiation triggers retrospective VAT assessment with a 10-year limitation period, default interest (normally 4% per annum), and penalties: intentional tax evasion carries a fine of up to 400% of the evaded tax, negligent evasion up to 100%; fabrication of export documents or circular/fictitious export schemes constitutes criminal tax fraud. Additionally, input VAT deductions are clawed back and affected invoices are invalidated. Switzerland does not impose a statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for VAT zero-rating; the 180-day benchmark is used as documentary repatriation diligence and for internal audit evidence.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB), Amtshaus Börsenstrasse, Zurich; together with the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) and the Federal Customs Administration (FCA) for trade payment statistics and export declarations; exchange controls are administered by the SNB within the framework of Switzerland's liberal capital account regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains a fully convertible hard-currency regime for both current and capital account transactions. There are no exchange controls, no mandatory centralised approval for cross-border payments, and no profit remittance restrictions for the current account or for direct investment income. Dividends and branch profits of a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft (AG) may be freely remitted abroad, subject only to the standard 35% Swiss federal withholding tax on dividends if the payment is deemed to have a Swiss source; the withholding tax can be reduced or avoided where a tax treaty or the Swiss participation relief applies. Capital repatriation on liquidation or capital redemption likewise faces no convertibility hurdle. The only practical constraints arise from AML/KYC documentation, the Swiss stamp duty on Swiss securities account turnover, and the SNB's Balance of Payments statistical reporting triggers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or forced conversion obligation exists. Swiss exporters may retain 100% of export proceeds in any currency and hold them offshore or onshore. There is no timeline within which receipts must be converted into CHF, and no mandatory conversion ratio. The only compliance requirement is statistical: a Swiss-resident enterprise is required to report to the Swiss National Bank, under the SNB's Ordinance on the Collection of Statistical Data on Payments with Foreign Countries and on Claims and Liabilities to Foreign Countries, if cross-border payment turnover with foreign counterparties exceeds CHF 10 million annually. Reporting is aggregated by category and is not a permission process. Export documents must comply with the Federal Customs Administration's electronic export declaration system (NCTS) for Swiss exports; customs documents are not tied to FX conversion.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / CHF-EUR-USD multi-currency cash management
Operational Account / Trade Finance & Commercial LC Desk
Operational Account / Regional SME treasury account
Operational Account / Payment and collection clearing via Swiss digital post office
Capital Escrow / Securities collateral account for treasury hedging

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for a regulated Swiss operational treasury account. Offshore digital EMI platforms (e.g. neobank or electronic money institution licensed in the EU/UK) do not generally hold a Swiss banking licence under Art. 1 of the Swiss Banking Act and cannot legally provide deposit-taking or payment services to a Swiss AG as a substitute for a licensed Swiss bank. A CHF settlement account must reside with a Swiss-regulated bank or a FINMA-licensed FinTech bank; however, a Swiss AG may use offshore EMIs as auxiliary disbursement rails for non-CHF supplier payments provided (i) the account is clearly sub-contracted and not the primary treasury account, (ii) the EMI does not hold funds in Switzerland on the Swiss entity's behalf in an unauthorised manner, and (iii) the head office bank grants a written crypto/liquidity-neutral consent. FINMA's FinTech licence allows deposit-taking up to CHF 1 million without interest, but it remains a Swiss-regulated entity, not an offshore EMI.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a foreign-owned, B2B MRO e-commerce AG with a registered office in Zug or Zurich and no statutory licence, physical presence of at least one natural person (the authorised signatory or UBO) is generally mandatory at a bank's Swiss branch for first-time account opening. A face-to-face interview with the relationship manager is standard for entities with any PEP exposure or with final beneficial owners in non-Swiss, non-EU countries, and it is always required where complex corporate structures are involved. Remote onboarding is exceptionally permitted for low-risk, standard commercial entities where the bank has adopted FINMA-supervised digital identification, but most established Tier-1 banks still require (a) a notarised and apostilled board resolution, (b) certified copy passport, (c) extraction from the Swiss commercial registry for the CH-AG and equivalent foreign registry excerpt for the ultimate parent, and (d) courier shipping of signed and notarised signature cards. For highest assurance, one director should appear physically at the bank's premises in Zurich or Zug.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-Swiss ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) with no demonstrable economic or commercial substance identifiable from the Swiss registry
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Swiss commercial registry excerpt (Handelsregister), UBO declaration signed by all shareholders, a copy of the consolidated organisational chart showing the industrial MRO procurement group, board minutes confirming the Swiss AG's operational role, and a physical office lease with Swiss utility bills; must evidence that the AG undertakes actual purchasing, warehousing, invoicing, and payment throughput rather than acting as a mere pass-through shell.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicious source of funds for the initial share capital contribution (CHF 100,000 minimum)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Up-to-90-day bank statements of the contributing parent account (showing commercial income), executed capital contribution agreement, SWIFT confirmation referencing the inbound purpose code, corporate tax statements from a competent foreign tax authority, and a written explanation of the funding chain from sale of inventory to capital transfer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Negative media or reputational press on the corporate or any UBO for customs duty evasion, sanctions against consumer goods, or intellectual property infringement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent legal opinion from a Swiss or EU law firm stating no engagement in prohibited trade; export classification certificates for MRO supplies; statement of all sanctioned country counterparties = zero; decree prohibiting self-funding of terrorism; and a compliance undertaking signed by the board of directors to maintain a sanctions screening register.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear payment-pattern expectation for a B2B low-risk profile, especially where supplier jurisdictions are in non-FATF-compliant zones
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction surveillance procedure manual, list of expected counterparty countries and bank counterparties, trade invoice templates, bill of lading or shipment documents for goods, and a published anti-money-laundering policy approved by the board designating the final AML officer; this addresses concern of layering and fornecedor-payee mismatch.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For any capital contribution from the non-resident parent to the Swiss AG, use a SWIFT MT103 in CHF/EUR/USD to the Swiss AG's preferred Tier-1 bank account. The wire must contain the business purpose narration precisely: 'Non-resident parent direct investment capital contribution to Swiss subsidiary; BOP direction: inbound; purpose code D/CAP (Direct Investment Equity Capital)' to avoid misclassification by the Swiss National Bank's statistics. The amount must be credited to a designated capital reserve account or a free capital account and posted in the AG's books against a contribution reserve, with the bank receiving the SWIFT confirmation. If the bank queries the source of wealth, provide the same evidence bundle as in the AML blockage defence. The transaction is reportable to the SNB in the quarterly balance-of-payments report if the entity exceeds the reporting threshold. There is no mandatory conversion or repatriation requirement; the funds can remain in EUR until the company's treasury policy converts to CHF via a standard market rate spot or forward transaction.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier settlements for industrial MRO supplies must be routed through the primary cleared rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for open-account payments to EU and global suppliers; (ii) SWIFT MT700 for irrevocable documentary letters of credit (L/C) where purchases exceed CHF 500,000 or require customs-backed security; (iii) SEPA CT in EUR when the supplier is EU/EEA-based, using the Swiss SEPA channel through a Swiss correspondent; (iv) SIC (Swiss Interbank Clearing) for urgent CHF domestic payments; and (v) the RTGS/CHATS US-dollar correspondent for USD settlements after FX conversion. Every outward payment must carry a valid foreign-trade purpose code: goods purchases (PUR), industrial supplies (MRO), or service fees (SRV), as required by the SNB statistical ordinance. L/Cs must be opened by a Swiss domestic bank with full recourse to the operational account, and the bill of lading / commercial document package must be kept in a secure treasury vault for audit by the Swiss Federal Tax Administration and FINMA if required.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright CHF/EUR/USD foreign-exchange forward contracts with a licensed Swiss bank (deliverable, no restriction on tenor)
CHF/FX currency swaps for rolling operating capital obligations, subject to the bank's ordinary ISDA or Swiss Master Agreement
Spot contracts for trade settlement timing adjustments and invoice settlement

Over-the-counter knock-in or knock-out barrier forwards for containment of high-volume MRO import exposures, provided the bank has derivative trading approval under the Swiss Financial Market Infrastructure Act (FMIA)

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on third-country emerging-market currencies used for purchasing MRO parts from Asia, cleared via a Swiss or London bank counterparty, as CHF itself is fully convertible and does not require an NDF market

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss Federal and Cantonal Corporate Income and Capital Tax Return together with Annual Financial Statements (Jahresrechnung)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Authority (Kantonale Steuerverwaltung) and Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung – ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual general meeting must approve the financial statements within six months of the balance sheet date; tax return must be filed within the cantonal deadline, typically six to nine months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties up to 30% of the assessed tax, mandatory interest on tax arrears, and criminal fines for misrepresentation; prolonged default may lead to enforcement proceedings and compulsory liquidation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting Minutes and Record of Adopted Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' Meeting (internal corporate body); a copy of the approved accounts is transmitted to the Cantonal Tax Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: General meeting must be held within six months of the balance sheet date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directorial liability for damages and administrative fines for failure to convene the meeting; the tax authority may assess taxable income based on the company's assumed records

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual or Quarterly Swiss Value Added Tax (VAT) Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filing by the sixtieth day after the fiscal period; quarterly filing by the end of the month following the quarter, subject to FIN-ESTV permitted filing cycles
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of 5% per annum, administrative fine up to 30% of the unpaid tax, and criminal penalties for deliberate non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Confirmation and Share Register Review Record
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No external annual filing – maintained at the registered office and available for inspection by MROS (Swiss Financial Intelligence Unit), criminal authorities, or the competent commercial register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous obligation; annual board-level review to be documented at the year-end meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under the Swiss AML Act up to CHF 500,000; personal criminal exposure for non-compliant directors

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory ordinary audit under Swiss Code of Obligations art. 727 if two of the following thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive financial years: total assets above CHF 20 million; net turnover above CHF 40 million; average annual full-time employees above 250. Where none of these apply, a limited audit is compulsory if two of the following thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive financial years: total assets above CHF 2 million; net turnover above CHF 4 million; average annual full-time employees above 10. Joint shareholders representing at least 10% of the share capital may force an audit regardless of thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss GAAP as set out in the Swiss Code of Obligations (OR 957–963); Swiss GAAP FER permitted as an accepted interpretative framework; IFRS required for listed entities and commonly adopted for significant consolidated groups

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland does not maintain a public or annually filed ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) register. The Aktiengesellschaft must continuously maintain an internal register of qualified beneficial owners under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act, update it upon any transfer or change of ownership control, and report details to MROS or another authorised authority upon request. The annual board review and any changes are recorded in the year-end documentation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Aktienregister / Register of Shareholders)
Minute Book for General Meetings and Board Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CHF 800 – CHF 2,500 per annum (USD 900 – USD 2,800) depending on canton and registered agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CHF 3,500 – CHF 8,000 for a limited audit (USD 4,000 – USD 9,000); CHF 8,000 – CHF 25,000 for an ordinary audit (USD 9,000 – USD 28,000) depending on turnover and complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% of net profit (effective federal rate approximately 7.83% on pre-tax profit); combined federal, cantonal and communal headline rate ranges from approximately 11.9% to 21.0% depending on the canton.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory corporate tax holiday exists in Switzerland. Notable incentives are granted at cantonal/communal level: patent box (up to 90% of qualifying patent income relieved), R&D super-deduction (extra deduction up to 50% of qualifying Swiss R&D costs), and notional interest deduction on surplus equity. At federal level, participation relief applies to qualifying dividend and capital-gain income from substantial participations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cantonal combined tax return for legal entities (German: Steuererklärung für juristische Personen; French: Déclaration fiscale pour personnes morales), used simultaneously for federal direct tax, cantonal/communal corporate income tax, and net wealth tax. Filing is made with the competent Cantonal Tax Administration; official electronic filing is available through each canton's approved tax e-filing portal or by paper submission.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing of the corporate income tax return; provisional prepayment instalments are generally required quarterly or in some cantons monthly.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual tax return is due within the canton's prescribed period after the statutory fiscal year end; for a calendar-year taxpayer this is normally 30 June of the following year. Extensions are commonly granted to 30 September or 31 December upon request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 1a / Box 1: Net profit before tax (Reingewinn / bénéfice net)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the net profit per the Swiss statutory annual financial statements prepared under the Swiss Code of Obligations, before appropriations to reserves and before dividend distributions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Swiss AG is the taxpayer and files the return. A non-resident shareholder does not report the Swiss AG's profit; only a foreign company with a Swiss permanent establishment is required to file a separate Swiss return for the PE-attributable profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 1b / Box 2: Tax adjustments for non-deductible expenses and hidden distributions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add back non-deductible expense items such as corporate income taxes, excessive management and royalty fees, non-depreciated disallowed construction costs, private portions, and hidden value transfers to shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjustments are made in the Swiss AG's return. Non-resident shareholders should not amend the AG's filing; any constructive dividend resulting from excessive payments is taken into account for Swiss withholding tax purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 2a / Box 8: Participation deduction, patent box and R&D super-deduction
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter qualifying federal participation relief on dividend and capital gains from substantial participations and, where the canton applies them, patent box relief and R&D super-deduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: These reliefs are available only to the Swiss resident AG and are not transferable to a foreign parent. The foreign parent's domestic tax treatment of Swiss-source dividends is governed by its residence country.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset available prior-year tax losses in chronological order, limited to the seven-year statutory carryforward period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses realised by the Swiss AG may be carried forward; losses of the foreign parent or affiliated group entities cannot be set off in the Swiss return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 4 / Box 12: Final taxable profit and tax computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare the adjusted taxable profit used by the tax authority to compute federal, cantonal and communal corporate taxes and net wealth tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident entity with no Swiss PE, no entry is made. For a non-resident entity with a Swiss PE, the Swiss PE profit must be shown on a separate non-resident corporate return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or incomplete filing triggers a reminder and an administrative default penalty (Ordnungsbusse) of up to CHF 10,000 under federal direct tax law, plus cantonal procedural surcharges. Late-payment interest accrues at statutory rates of approximately 3% to 5% per annum. Knowingly or negligently filing false returns gives rise to an evasion penalty of up to three times the evaded tax, in addition to reassessment and interest.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% statutory withholding tax on dividends distributed by a Swiss AG, withheld at source; treaty relief for qualifying non-resident shareholders is implemented mainly by refund after withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Swiss paying company withholds 35% at source. The non-resident beneficial owner must file a refund application with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC) on the official withholding tax refund form, attaching: (i) a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the home-country tax authority covering the income year; (ii) the dividend voucher/statement and proof of source withholding; and (iii) a beneficial ownership declaration. The claim must generally be made within three years after the income falls due. The shareholder must satisfy the applicable DTA's residence, beneficial ownership, and anti-abuse or limitation-on-benefits clauses; a mere TRC without economic substance is insufficient.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: no Swiss statutory withholding tax on IP royalties; treaty rates generally range from 0% to 10%. Interest: statutory 35% withholding tax applies to certain Swiss-source debt income, principally Swiss bank interest and Swiss bond/debenture interest, while ordinary intercompany loan interest is generally outside the Swiss withholding tax net; treaty rates for debt interest typically range from 0% to 10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Swiss transfer pricing documentation duty under Art. 174a DBG applies when annual gross turnover reaches at least CHF 10 million and the taxpayer has cross-border transactions with related parties. In practice, a Local File is expected for related-party transactions exceeding approximately CHF 1 million; a Master File is generally expected for group consolidated revenue above CHF 100 million under Federal Tax Administration guidance.
